title: Personal Checking: Grounds for Refunding a Fee — Bank Error and Courtesy
content:
## General clause

Any Personal Checking fee that is refunded is refunded whole, never partly, through a single refund entry that names the fee as its source and equals that fee's amount. A fee can be refunded only once. Two grounds exist, and the bank-error ground is examined ahead of the courtesy ground.

## Bank-error ground

A fee is a bank error when it was charged in a way the Personal Checking charter does not allow. Examples: a maintenance fee for a cycle in which a waiver was met; an overdraft fee past the tier's daily fee count, on an item at or below the small-item threshold, or on a day within the end-of-day threshold; or any fee charged at an amount different from the tier's published figure. A bank-error refund has no time limit and never uses up any courtesy allowance.

## Courtesy ground

A courtesy refund is a goodwill refund of a fee that was charged correctly. It may be granted only if every one of these holds:

- **Fee kind.** The fee is a monthly maintenance fee, a paper statement fee, an overdraft item fee, a returned item fee, an extended overdraft fee, an overdraft protection transfer fee or a non-PCB domestic ATM fee.
- **Posting age.** The fee posted no more than the tier's courtesy window, in calendar days, before the refund is granted. The day after the fee's posting date is day 1, and the refund is allowed on any date up to and including the posting date plus the window.
- **Yearly allowance.** The customer's courtesy refunds within the rolling 365 days that end on the current date, both ends included, number fewer than the tier's yearly allowance. The count covers every checking account the customer holds, with each refunded fee counting as one.
- **Account status.** The account is active when the courtesy refund is granted.

The courtesy window and allowance applied are those of the tier on the account on the current date. All of these facts are read from the bank's records.

When the customer asks for more eligible fees than the allowance leaves room for, the most recently posted fees are refunded ahead of older ones, and among fees posted on the same day the larger fee goes ahead of the smaller.

## Outside this rule

A refund made when a dispute is settled in the owner's favour is governed by the dispute rules and is not a courtesy refund. This rule does not cover requests to give back interest, a charged-off balance or fees levied by another bank.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical window of 45 days)

| Fee posted | Date of the request | Within window? |
|---|---|---|
| 10 January 2026 | 24 February 2026 (day 45) | yes |
| 10 January 2026 | 25 February 2026 (day 46) | no |

## Allowance illustration (hypothetical)

A customer on a tier allowing two courtesy refunds a year already received one, eight months ago, on another checking account. One more may be granted now. If the customer asks about three eligible fees, the one posted most recently is refunded.
